articles.title: Tech picks: Indian Hotels among 5 stocks to buy for healthy returns in short term
articles.desc: The Indian stock market is rebounding, powered by robust investments in IT sectors and encouraging earnings reports. Analysts highlight five stocks as prime buying opportunities, projecting solid short-term gains. Indian Hotels, Lemon Tree, and Supreme Industries make the list. While technical indicators show strong demand, investors are cautioned about looming global inflation and geopolitical tensions.

articles.title: Stock Market Down: Bulls lose ground! Sensex sinks nearly 900 points, Nifty ends below 22,900; 5 key triggers behind Rs 5 lakh crore selloff
articles.desc: Why is  Market Down Today: The Indian stock market took a hit on Monday after a considerable rise the previous week. Both Sensex and Nifty struggled, with Axis Bank and HDFC Bank suffering significant losses. However, firms like SBI and UltraTech Cement managed to post gains. The PSU Bank index rose, providing a stark contrast to the declining private banking sector.

articles.title: Holding company discount after Jio IPO: What is it & how will it impact RIL shares?
articles.desc: Jio Platforms IPO: Jio Platforms is preparing to unveil its initial public offering, enhancing its valuation significantly. Analysts foresee a potential reduction in the holding company discount for Reliance Industries post-IPO. While some experts believe the anticipated changes are already included in the stock's valuation, the true effect on RIL shares will hinge on Jio's profitability and future dividend plans.

articles.title: Global Market: South Korean shares fall as AI investment worries weigh on chipmakers
articles.desc: South Korea’s Kospi fell as AI investment concerns triggered technology stock selling, although dip buying helped recover early losses. Semiconductor shares remained weak, while automakers, battery makers and select heavyweight stocks gained. Foreign investors were net sellers, while currency and bond markets showed mixed movements amid ongoing global market uncertainty.

articles.title: Exporters may be asked to monitor supply chains' indirect emissions
articles.desc: The Indian government is engaging in discussions about measuring Scope 3 emissions for exporters. This consideration arises as trade partners impose tighter green requirements globally. Current frameworks focus on direct emissions and exclude indirect ones, making compliance more complex. As a result, industries, especially MSMEs, may face compliance burdens if new requirements are implemented. Ultimately, the aim is to ensure that Indian exporters remain competitive in international markets.

articles.title: Farmers face 15% loss as poultry feed costs surge
articles.desc: Poultry farmers are currently experiencing losses of approximately 15% due to rising livestock feed costs. Key ingredients have seen price increases of up to 75%, affecting farmers' ability to cope. Dairy producers, particularly in drought-affected regions, struggle to source necessary fodder for their livestock. Feed manufacturers are also feeling the impact as higher prices reduce demand for their products.

articles.title: Global investors against use of judicial anti-avoidance rule by tax officials
articles.desc: International investors have raised concerns regarding the Indian Income-tax authorities' invocation of the judicial anti-avoidance rule. At a recent meeting, investors communicated their issues with the Central Board of Direct Taxes on this matter. The use of JAAR to deny relief on grandfathered shares contradicts prior regulations established by the CBDT. The standing of both GAAR and JAAR remains complex due to Supreme Court rulings.
